complete_independent_native_report.report:
PASS applies only to the restricted A–F candidate. Original P09 completion remains false; this audit does not change any earlier native verdict or completion count. The mathematical argument is self-contained under the task’s permitted foundations.

Conventions and normalization. Scaling γ by t>0 multiplies Aθ, Ah and Dμ by t^(n−1), so normalization preserves both quotients and the Gauduchon condition. In an h-unitary frame, let G represent γ and C=(det G)G^−1. Then det C=(det G)^(n−1). Diagonalizing G gives γ^n=(det G)h^n and θ∧γ^(n−1)=tr(θC)h^n/n for every Hermitian θ: off-diagonal entries of θ contribute zero in that frame. Unitary invariance proves the identity for arbitrary matrices, without simultaneous diagonalization. Substituting μ=rh^n/H therefore gives Ah=(H/n)∫tr C dν and Dμ=H^((n−1)/n)∫r^(1/n)(det C)^(1/n)dν. These constants are correct.

A. Constant rank gives smooth kernel and positive spectral subbundles, with orthogonal projections Q and P. The spectral hypothesis gives B≥δP. For an arbitrary positive C, write C=[[U,V],[V*,W]] in the Q,P splitting. Its Schur complement S=W−V*U^−1V is positive: evaluate the quadratic form of C on (−U^−1Vv,v). Block elimination gives det C=det U det S. Since W^−1/2SW^−1/2 is positive and at most the identity, det S≤det W. Arithmetic–geometric mean consequently gives det C≤(s/m)^m(p/q)^q, where s=tr U=tr(QC)>0 and p=tr W=tr(PC)>0. This explicitly retains V and controls every nondiagonal test.

Put z=∫p dν and y=Hz/n. Normalization gives ∫s dν=n/H−z and 0<y<1. Moreover, tr((B−δP)C)≥0 because C^(1/2)(B−δP)C^(1/2) is semipositive. Hence e≥δy. To check the integral step, put S0=∫s dν and P0=∫p dν. Weighted arithmetic–geometric mean applied pointwise to s/S0 and p/P0, with weights m/n and q/n, yields ∫s^(m/n)p^(q/n)dν≤S0^(m/n)P0^(q/n). Together with r≤R, this gives Dμ≤n(R/H)^(1/n)((1−y)/m)^(m/n)(y/q)^(q/n). The logarithmic derivative of (1−y)^(m/n)y^(q/n) is (q−ny)/(ny(1−y)). Thus replacement of y by e/δ is justified precisely on the stated range 0<e≤δq/n. Dropping (1−e/δ)^(m/n) gives the claimed uniform O(e^(q/n)) bound. No Gauduchon or invariance restriction enters this upper estimate.

B. Under its explicit hypothesis κh(α)=a, a normalized threshold-minimizing sequence has ej=AB(γj)=Aα(γj)−a→0. Each ej is strictly positive because B has positive rank and Cj is positive. Eventually ej≤δq/n, so A applies with a constant independent of j and proves the asserted denominator collapse. The proof does not infer κ=a from α≥ah. In the torus application, equality is established separately below. No general Gauduchon existence theorem is needed for this conditional assertion.

C. On E one can take ω=(i/2)dz∧dbar z=dx∧dy, which descends to the quotient, is closed, and has integral one. Its factor pullbacks satisfy ωi²=0 and commute under wedge product. Consequently μ is a probability volume, h^n=n!μ, and α^n=Mμ with M=n!a^m(a+δ)^q. Both h and α are closed and strictly positive, and α≥ah. Nefness follows directly from the usual definition: the zero potential gives α+D0≥−εh for every ε>0. Bigness is explicit as well: the smooth closed current T=α satisfies T≥ah. No closed-nef bigness theorem is invoked. The actual top intersection is ∫α^n=M>0.

D. Here H=n!, ν=μ, R=1, and B=δP. Therefore y=e/δ exactly, so the determinant and integral estimates above give the requested upper bound for every 0<e<δ, without using the restricted monotonicity step. These are also the exact admissible excess bounds: positivity of both blocks forces 0<AB<δAh for every positive test.

For attainment, put x=e/δ, wi=(1−x)/m on the first block and wi=x/q on the second, and ci=wi/(n−1)!. Set C=diag(ci), T=(det C)^(1/(n−1)), and γe=T∑ci^−1ωi. This is an actual smooth positive closed metric for every x∈(0,1). Its matrix is G=TC^−1. Direct calculation gives det G=T^n/det C=T and (det G)G^−1=C, verifying the full inverse-cofactor construction. Its pairings are Ah=(n−1)!∑ci=1 and AB=δ(n−1)!∑i>m ci=e. Its denominator is (n!)^((n−1)/n)(det C)^(1/n)=[n/(n!)^(1/n)](∏wi)^(1/n), exactly the asserted value. Closedness implies D(γe^(n−1))=0; the factor i/(2π) introduces no additional constant. Thus the bound is an attained maximum over all normalized Gauduchon tests. The endpoints e=0 and e=δ are inadmissible for positive tests, although the maximum profile tends to zero there.

For κ, semipositivity gives Aα/Ah≥a for every test, while the metrics γe satisfy Aα=a+e and e can tend to zero. Hence κh(α)=a; the infimum is not attained by a positive metric. For λ, the eigenvalues of α relative to an arbitrary positive γ give α∧γ^(n−1)≥(α^n/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n by arithmetic–geometric mean, including the trace factor 1/n. Since α^n=Mμ, integration yields Aα≥M^(1/n)Dμ for every positive test. The closed Gauduchon metric γ=α attains equality: Aα(α)=M and Dμ(α)=M^((n−1)/n). Therefore λμ(α)=M^(1/n), using the full Gauduchon class.

E. Every normalized threshold-minimizing sequence has Aα→a>0 and Dμ→0 by B or D, despite positive κ, λ and top intersection and the explicit big representative. Its root-volume quotient actually tends to infinity. Conversely, normalizing γ=α gives cofactor weights wi=ai^−1/∑aℓ^−1, where ai=a or a+δ. Its excess is δ[q/(a+δ)]/[m/a+q/(a+δ)]=δqa/(na+mδ)>0. Thus this root-volume minimizer does not minimize the threshold quotient. The comparison with the nonbig conditional requires no external nonbigness theorem: its required normalized limit Aα→0 is impossible here, since Aα≥a. Denominator collapse alone supplies no such antecedent.

F. The example disproves universal availability of a normalized threshold-minimizing sequence with positive denominator lower limit, even for this closed positive background. It does not contradict closed-nef positive-intersection bigness, establish the general root-volume bridge, or complete original P09.

Harmless wording clarifications: the common scaling factor is t^(n−1); “cofactor endomorphism” here means the adjugate (det G)G^−1, rather than an untransposed array of signed minors; and “remains open” should be read as “is not settled by this argument.” Current literature-wide openness is not certified. The three cited versioned manuscript files returned 404 on attempted retrieval, including their raw-file counterparts. Their definitions are already supplied by the task, and no cited theorem is indispensable to the reconstructed proof. Accordingly, no nonroutine external premise or source passage is used.
